So after having it on my list forever, yesterday morning I finished The Road. I have to say, this is an amazing book. The ending was superb, and now I'm looking for more truly gritty post-apocalyptic fiction. I'm a huge fan of The Dark Tower series and I've read 70 or so of the Deathlands books so far, but The Road left me craving something with that true realism. Any recommendations?
Just finished reading The Road, finally
Have you read The Stand? If you're a big fan of The Dark Tower then The Stand seems like an obvious choice.
Oh yeah, I've read most of King's works. I've always considered The Stand to be a tangential part of the Dark Tower series, much like Eyes of the Dragon.

It's not exactly gritty, but On the Beach is an excellent book about people in Melbourne who are still alive after a nuclear war and know that radiation is slowly bearing down on them. Really enjoyed reading it.

You should also try "One Second After" or "Lights Out". They deal with the aftermath of the total breakdown of civilization after a EMP attack. Neither book goes into detail on the actual event (much like The Road), but squarely focus on the survivors.
Those both sound pretty much right in line with what I'm looking for. Is there one you'd recommend over the other, or which to read first?
I'd go with "Lights Out" first, I'd say its a bit more uplifting (as much as this genre can be) :)
